review_scope: Bounded FC-089 candidate and necessary neighbouring distinctions; other established interpretations preserved.
research_method: Canonical occurrence source packet plus relevant joint searches in RESEARCH-LEDGER.json; inaccessible historical contracts remain unknown, not unperformed research.

access_limit: The public status report does not disclose which component of the Microsoft/OpenAI federated authentication exchange failed or why.
Posts are first-person user testimony and do not expose provider telemetry or the internal token-exchange implementation.
Fallback conditions differ between users: one user retained smartphone access while another reported that trying Google sign-in did not restore access to the affected account.

occurrence_evidence.claim: On 5 June at 14:48, OpenAI investigated Microsoft personal-account sign-in failure affecting API and ChatGPT Login. It distinguished that route from general account access.

Contemporaneous community users reported token-exchange errors on Microsoft-linked paid accounts. One retained smartphone access despite browser failure; another said Google sign-in did not restore access. Forum and status timestamps are not forced into one timezone.
At 15:24, OpenAI reported applied mitigation and monitored recovery.
At 15:58 it reported all impacted services recovered.

Later forum posts described restored login with missing paid entitlements, deletion messages or inconsistent usage limits. A moderator acknowledged subscription investigation. These are individual reports, not provider-confirmed uniform continuation of the sign-in outage.

evidence_summary: Microsoft sign-in disruption affected some paid accounts; later account and subscription reports do not prove an uninterrupted common cause.
unestablished_fact_or_limit: The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.
criterion_tests.reason: The independently applicable duty and threshold are not established: The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: Microsoft sign-in disruption affected some paid accounts; later account and subscription reports do not prove an uninterrupted common cause. The shortfall relative to a governed threshold cannot be determined without the missing obligation.

criterion_tests.literal: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
criterion_tests.reason: The required response for this service cannot be inferred from the observed disruption: The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.
criterion_tests.reason: No finding that actual mitigation failed an applicable standard is possible solely from this sequence: Microsoft sign-in disruption affected some paid accounts; later account and subscription reports do not prove an uninterrupted common cause.

criterion_tests.literal: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
criterion_tests.reason: Interference or distress is preserved, but impairment of specifically obligated use is not established: Microsoft sign-in disruption affected some paid accounts; later account and subscription reports do not prove an uninterrupted common cause.

criterion_tests.literal: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
criterion_tests.reason: The occurrence may engage continuity, but its independent obligation is unestablished: The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
criterion_tests.reason: Adequacy of an authorised response must be compared with that obligation; the observed response is: Microsoft sign-in disruption affected some paid accounts; later account and subscription reports do not prove an uninterrupted common cause.

criterion_tests.literal: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
criterion_tests.reason: No measured satisfaction of the required service level follows from the available endpoint or recovery report: The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: This is an evidence-state exclusion, not proof that no duty existed. The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate concerns service operation or withdrawal, rather than a single inaccurate output: Microsoft OAuth disruption.

criterion_tests.literal: A lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures.
criterion_tests.reason: The validity, proportionality and sufficient alternatives of the restriction/response must be evidenced separately; The affected sign-in entitlement and acceptable recovery/fallback terms.

criterion_tests.literal: A temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement; an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required.
criterion_tests.reason: Recovery adequacy or absence of a feasible required response is not established merely by eventual resolution: Microsoft sign-in disruption affected some paid accounts; later account and subscription reports do not prove an uninterrupted common cause.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate includes an actual function/access question, not only its description: Microsoft OAuth disruption.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
criterion_tests.reason: Verification may explain access but does not supply a broader obligation.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate is not solely durable or restored work-state loss: Microsoft OAuth disruption.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
criterion_tests.reason: No claim that an infrastructure concession was demanded is the basis of this availability candidate: Microsoft OAuth disruption.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
criterion_tests.reason: The proposed property concerns service function rather than only an interaction-level vulnerability response: Microsoft OAuth disruption.

neighbour_comparison: Identity dependency and subscription representation are distinct from an independently governed availability threshold.

prior_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: OpenAI identified Microsoft personal-account sign-in as the affected route, keeping that route's failure distinct from the user's wider account, entitlement or platform status. That accurate distinction is the bounded positive finding. Whether access survived through cached, degraded or alternate routes remains unresolved: the reports describe different outcomes across users and devices.

classification_review_provenance.review_status: Evidence-first HIM and relational/protection fidelity review; prior roles accounted for.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The provider distinctly identified Microsoft personal-account sign-in as the affected route rather than representing the incident as a generic account, entitlement or platform state. This successful-invariant finding is limited to that access-state distinction.
